bull_bear.body: No new capital-raise, dividend, or buyback discussed this call. CRAR 18.85% / Tier-1 17.27% — comfortably capitalized; an analyst explicitly noted the bank is "well capitalized" with room to accelerate growth further.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **CASA ratio ticked down QoQ (36.77%)** — the one guided metric the bank is not currently beating; worth tracking given the funding-cost implications of a rising CD ratio (82.29%, up sharply from 75.47% YoY).
- **ECL-transition gap** — ~22–30% of the assessed ~Rs 3,200cr+ requirement still to be provided before 1-Apr-2027, contingent on quarterly profitability.
- **Treasury under yield-hardening pressure** — limited by small FVTPL exposure, but a genuine headwind management flags explicitly.
- **TWO recovery normalizing to ~Rs 300cr/quarter** after exhausting the large one-off accounts — residual recovery will rely on smaller-ticket SARFAESI/OTS measures, a structurally lower-recovery regime going forward.
- **Formal guidance intentionally not revised** despite advances growth running at ~2x the guided band — if growth decelerates toward the stale 12–14% guide in H2, that would itself be a notable deceleration worth flagging, not merely "meeting guidance."
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: MD Rajendra Kumar Saboo is granular and consistent — walks through every guided metric against actual performance unprompted, directly explains the agri-seasonality behind the slippage uptick, and transparently breaks down the TWO recovery/ECL-provisioning bridges with exact rupee figures. He explicitly declines to speculate on PSU-bank merger rumors raised by an analyst and is firm (but transparent about the rationale) in refusing to formally revise guidance mid-year even when actual performance runs well ahead — a disciplined, non-promotional stance.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **Every quantitative guidance metric bar CASA ratio is being beaten by a wide margin**, yet management's refusal to revise guidance is a structural (board-process) choice, not a signal of caution about H2 — worth distinguishing from banks that under-guide opportunistically.
- **RAM share has already crossed its own upper guided bound (65%)** — management's framing ("we will be maintaining around 65% only") suggests corporate growth is intended to scale roughly in proportion going forward, not to dilute RAM mix.
- **ECL-transition provisioning is ~70–78% pre-funded already**, 18 months ahead of the April-2027 transition date — a conservative, de-risked posture relative to peers who may be provisioning later.
- **Second-hand car financing — flagged by the analyst as a differentiator vs other PSU banks — is explicitly not yet tracked separately by management**, despite being raised in back-to-back quarters; a genuine disclosure gap rather than evidence the business is immaterial.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Shareholding concentrated with Government at 90.95%, leaving a thin free float (DIIs 4.15%, Others 4.84%, FII 0.06%) as of 30.09.2026.
- FY27 capital plan blends fresh equity (up to Rs. 2700 Cr) and bonds (up to Rs. 5000 Cr) rather than relying only on internal accruals, indicating continued reliance on external capital to support growth/CRAR.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Retail (housing):** home-loan growth +20%+ YoY on both volume (more borrowers onboarded) and value (average ticket size up ~30%, from ~Rs 35 lakh to ~Rs 45 lakh).
- **Gold loan:** yield ~9%, unchanged QoQ; any EBLR-linked gold loans will reprice up with the repo hike.
- **Second-hand car financing:** acknowledged as a differentiated earlier-mover product (100–150bps yield premium over new-car loans) but not separately tracked — folded into consolidated vehicle-loan growth; management says it is "still a very small amount" of the overall car-loan book.
- **Treasury:** under pressure from hardening yields (incl. the RBI 25bp repo hike) but FVTPL book is "very, very controlled," so MTM losses are limited; NII gains from the 66%-EBLR-linked advances book are expected to more than offset any treasury drag.
- **GIFT City IBU:** opened this quarter, already "doing good business"; alongside Hong Kong and Singapore branches, management expects "reasonable growth" across all three overseas centers, not cannibalization.
- **Agriculture slippage:** Rs 205cr of the Rs 549cr total slippage this quarter (vs Rs 73cr in Jun-26 and Rs 238cr in Sep-25) — driven entirely by the **September half-yearly crop-loan classification marking**, a seasonal/structural pattern, not a quality deterioration (YoY actually improved).

- [Disclaimer] Presentation contains forward-looking statements subject to risks/uncertainties; Bank undertakes no obligation to update them after the stated date.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: NIM sustained above guidance (global 3.00% vs 2.80–2.90% guided) on repo-rate pass-through to the 66%-EBLR-linked book, with a lag effect expected before deposit costs catch up (management sees no immediate need to raise deposit rates). Cost-to-income at 50.39% reflects the true run-rate (Jun-26's lower ratio of ~45% ex-one-off recovery was distorted by the one-time Rs 785cr TWO recovery); full-year target ~50%, trending down from 52.79% in Sep-2025. Other operating expenses rose ~Rs 160cr QoQ — management calls this normal, reflecting IT and physical-infrastructure investment tied to business expansion, not a one-off.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q2 FY27 (this):** Advances +24.70% YoY (vs 12–14% guide); deposits +14.36% (vs 10–12%); net profit Rs 786cr (+26.77% YoY); GNPA 1.96% / NNPA 0.18% — both already inside FY27 targets; global NIM 3.00% (vs 2.80–2.90% guide); credit cost 0.65% (vs <0.75%); RAM share crossed 65%; CASA ratio dipped slightly to 36.77%; GIFT City IBU opened; ECL-transition provisioning ~70–78% pre-funded. Guidance formally unrevised despite being beaten across the board.
- _Q3 FY27 → check: CASA ratio trend; CD ratio (currently 82.29%) sustainability; deposit-rate repricing decision; corporate-book disbursement pace against the Rs 10,000cr sanctioned pipeline; TWO recovery holding near Rs 300cr/quarter; cost-to-income trending to ~50%; any FY27 guidance revision (unlikely per management's stated process, but worth re-checking)._
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)

outlook.body:
- **Advances growth: 12–14% (FY27, board-approved, unrevised)** — actual 24.70% YoY this quarter; management explicitly declined to raise the formal number when pressed by an analyst, but says it will "try to grow more than the guidance."
- **Deposit growth: 10–12% guided** — actual 14.36%.
- **GNPA <2% by 31-Mar-2027** — already at 1.96% at H1.
- **Net NPA <0.25% for the year** — already at 0.18% at H1.
- **Slippage ratio <1%** — actual 0.85% this quarter.
- **Credit cost <0.75% for FY27** — actual 0.65%, expected to stay within guidance for the year.
- **Global NIM 2.80–2.90% guided** — actual 3.00%, management expects to sustain above guidance as the repo-rate hike passes through the EBLR-linked book (66% of advances).
- **RAM share target 62–65%** — already crossed 65%; management intends to hold around this level going forward, letting corporate growth proceed in parallel.
- **Cost-to-income:** targeting ~50% for FY27 (down from 52.79% in Sep-2025), **<50% targeted for next year.**
- **ECL transition (1-Apr-2027):** assessed requirement ~Rs 3,200cr+; already provided Rs 2,500cr (≈70–78% of requirement, incl. Rs 530cr retained COVID provision + Rs 341cr extra provisioning + Rs 1,600cr+ ECL-specific); balance to be provided over coming quarters "as profitability permits."
- **TWO (written-off) recovery:** normalized run-rate ~Rs 300cr/quarter expected to continue (June quarter's Rs 1,018cr included a one-off Rs 785cr single-account recovery).
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body: ~Rs 10,000cr sanctioned-but-undisbursed corporate credit pipeline; disbursement pace contingent on corporate appetite at prevailing lending rates post the RBI 25bp repo hike. Management reiterates confidence in sustaining RAM-led growth (retail/agri/MSME) alongside resumed corporate book growth, without giving a specific forward number beyond the unrevised 12–14% guide.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **CBDC:** UCO Digital Rupee marketplace (ticket booking, gift cards, other payments via CBDC wallet) and CBDC IVR offline-access service launched this quarter.
- **RPA:** 7 processes automated.
- **Digital marketing solution** onboarded to grow the digital-business balance sheet (Project Parivartan), now **Rs 48,000+ crore.**
- **UPI:** Tap and Pay, Help 2.0, and an automatic VPA/QR-authenticity surveillance system launched.
- **Customer 360-degree portal** rolled out in branches for cross-sell; online self-service module for branch bookings.
- **eFDR on MCX** launched (already live on BSE/NSE) — brokers can now book eFDR via UCO Bank across all three exchanges.
- **CASA MOUs:** Government of Bihar (employee salary accounts) and empanelment with the Rajasthan state government for its salary-account package.

one-line thesis: Another quarter of guidance massively exceeded, not revised — advances grew 24.70% YoY vs a 12–14% guided band, net profit +26.77% YoY to Rs 786cr, and both GNPA (1.96%) and NNPA (0.18%) are already inside full-year targets at the half-year mark — yet management explicitly declined an analyst's direct suggestion to raise the formal guidance, citing board-approved annual targets that aren't revised mid-year. The quarter's one softer spot is CASA ratio (36.77%, down slightly QoQ), and slippages ticked up on the seasonal September agriculture-loan classification marking, not a credit-quality deterioration.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy): > RAM detail: Retail +30.23% YoY; Agriculture +29.59%; MSME +20.32%; overall RAM +26.92% YoY, portfolio Rs 1,68,736cr, RAM share crossed 65% (vs 62–65% guided). Corporate advances +24.15% YoY, Rs ~10,000cr sanctioned-not-disbursed pipeline. Business/employee Rs 30cr (vs Rs 25cr); business/branch Rs 185cr (vs Rs 161cr).
guidance (critical — verify next quarter: Advances growth: 12–14% (FY27, board-approved, unrevised) — actual 24.70% YoY this quarter; management explicitly declined to raise the formal number when pressed by an analyst, but says it will "try to grow more than the guidance."
Deposit growth: 10–12% guided — actual 14.36%.
GNPA <2% by 31-Mar-2027 — already at 1.96% at H1.
Net NPA <0.25% for the year — already at 0.18% at H1.
Slippage ratio <1% — actual 0.85% this quarter.
Credit cost <0.75% for FY27 — actual 0.65%, expected to stay within guidance for the year.
Global NIM 2.80–2.90% guided — actual 3.00%, management expects to sustain above guidance as the repo-rate hike passes through the EBLR-linked book (66% of advances).
RAM share target 62–65% — already crossed 65%; management intends to hold around this level going forward, letting corporate growth proceed in parallel.
Cost-to-income: targeting ~50% for FY27 (down from 52.79% in Sep-2025), <50% targeted for next year.

ECL transition (1-Apr-2027): assessed requirement ~Rs 3,200cr+; already provided Rs 2,500cr (≈70–78% of requirement, incl. Rs 530cr retained COVID provision + Rs 341cr extra provisioning + Rs 1,600cr+ ECL-specific); balance to be provided over coming quarters "as profitability permits."
TWO (written-off) recovery: normalized run-rate ~Rs 300cr/quarter expected to continue (June quarter's Rs 1,018cr included a one-off Rs 785cr single-account recovery).
order book & pipeline: ~Rs 10,000cr sanctioned-but-undisbursed corporate credit pipeline; disbursement pace contingent on corporate appetite at prevailing lending rates post the RBI 25bp repo hike. Management reiterates confidence in sustaining RAM-led growth (retail/agri/MSME) alongside resumed corporate book growth, without giving a specific forward number beyond the unrevised 12–14% guide.
segment / subsidiary detail: Retail (housing): home-loan growth +20%+ YoY on both volume (more borrowers onboarded) and value (average ticket size up ~30%, from ~Rs 35 lakh to ~Rs 45 lakh).
Gold loan: yield ~9%, unchanged QoQ; any EBLR-linked gold loans will reprice up with the repo hike.

Second-hand car financing: acknowledged as a differentiated earlier-mover product (100–150bps yield premium over new-car loans) but not separately tracked — folded into consolidated vehicle-loan growth; management says it is "still a very small amount" of the overall car-loan book.

Treasury: under pressure from hardening yields (incl. the RBI 25bp repo hike) but FVTPL book is "very, very controlled," so MTM losses are limited; NII gains from the 66%-EBLR-linked advances book are expected to more than offset any treasury drag.

GIFT City IBU: opened this quarter, already "doing good business"; alongside Hong Kong and Singapore branches, management expects "reasonable growth" across all three overseas centers, not cannibalization.

Agriculture slippage: Rs 205cr of the Rs 549cr total slippage this quarter (vs Rs 73cr in Jun-26 and Rs 238cr in Sep-25) — driven entirely by the September half-yearly crop-loan classification marking, a seasonal/structural pattern, not a quality deterioration (YoY actually improved).
growth verticals / optionality: CBDC: UCO Digital Rupee marketplace (ticket booking, gift cards, other payments via CBDC wallet) and CBDC IVR offline-access service launched this quarter.
Digital marketing solution onboarded to grow the digital-business balance sheet (Project Parivartan), now Rs 48,000+ crore.
UPI: Tap and Pay, Help 2.0, and an automatic VPA/QR-authenticity surveillance system launched.
Customer 360-degree portal rolled out in branches for cross-sell; online self-service module for branch bookings.
eFDR on MCX launched (already live on BSE/NSE) — brokers can now book eFDR via UCO Bank across all three exchanges.
CASA MOUs: Government of Bihar (employee salary accounts) and empanelment with the Rajasthan state government for its salary-account package.
margins & cost dynamics: NIM sustained above guidance (global 3.00% vs 2.80–2.90% guided) on repo-rate pass-through to the 66%-EBLR-linked book, with a lag effect expected before deposit costs catch up (management sees no immediate need to raise deposit rates). Cost-to-income at 50.39% reflects the true run-rate (Jun-26's lower ratio of ~45% ex-one-off recovery was distorted by the one-time Rs 785cr TWO recovery); full-year target ~50%, trending down from 52.79% in Sep-2025. Other operating expenses rose ~Rs 160cr QoQ — management calls this normal, reflecting IT and physical-infrastructure investment tied to business expansion, not a one-off.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): Branch network expanded to 3,439 (+27 branches this quarter). GIFT City IFSC branch opened and already generating business. No numeric capex figure disclosed for IT/digital infrastructure spend (described qualitatively as rising "other operating expenses").
capital allocation: No new capital-raise, dividend, or buyback discussed this call. CRAR 18.85% / Tier-1 17.27% — comfortably capitalized; an analyst explicitly noted the bank is "well capitalized" with room to accelerate growth further.
risks & watch-items: CASA ratio ticked down QoQ (36.77%) — the one guided metric the bank is not currently beating; worth tracking given the funding-cost implications of a rising CD ratio (82.29%, up sharply from 75.47% YoY).
ECL-transition gap — ~22–30% of the assessed ~Rs 3,200cr+ requirement still to be provided before 1-Apr-2027, contingent on quarterly profitability.
Treasury under yield-hardening pressure — limited by small FVTPL exposure, but a genuine headwind management flags explicitly.

TWO recovery normalizing to ~Rs 300cr/quarter after exhausting the large one-off accounts — residual recovery will rely on smaller-ticket SARFAESI/OTS measures, a structurally lower-recovery regime going forward.

Formal guidance intentionally not revised despite advances growth running at ~2x the guided band — if growth decelerates toward the stale 12–14% guide in H2, that would itself be a notable deceleration worth flagging, not merely "meeting guidance."
management quality / tone: MD Rajendra Kumar Saboo is granular and consistent — walks through every guided metric against actual performance unprompted, directly explains the agri-seasonality behind the slippage uptick, and transparently breaks down the TWO recovery/ECL-provisioning bridges with exact rupee figures. He explicitly declines to speculate on PSU-bank merger rumors raised by an analyst and is firm (but transparent about the rationale) in refusing to formally revise guidance mid-year even when actual performance runs well ahead — a disciplined, non-promotional stance.
non-obvious takeaways: Every quantitative guidance metric bar CASA ratio is being beaten by a wide margin, yet management's refusal to revise guidance is a structural (board-process) choice, not a signal of caution about H2 — worth distinguishing from banks that under-guide opportunistically.

RAM share has already crossed its own upper guided bound (65%) — management's framing ("we will be maintaining around 65% only") suggests corporate growth is intended to scale roughly in proportion going forward, not to dilute RAM mix.
ECL-transition provisioning is ~70–78% pre-funded already, 18 months ahead of the April-2027 transition date — a conservative, de-risked posture relative to peers who may be provisioning later.

Second-hand car financing — flagged by the analyst as a differentiator vs other PSU banks — is explicitly not yet tracked separately by management, despite being raised in back-to-back quarters; a genuine disclosure gap rather than evidence the business is immaterial.
